topic.source_contract: Land-contamination planning, source-pathway-receptor, remediation and verification evidence

facts.planning: planning should ensure land is suitable for its new use and unacceptable risk is prevented
facts.assessment: proportionate competent-person risk assessment identifies sources, pathways and receptors
facts.guard: suspected contamination is not proof of statutory contaminated land or successful remediation

facts.scope: risk-based guidance covers human health, controlled waters, ecology, gases and property
facts.planning: most redevelopment contamination is addressed through planning
facts.guard: screening values or one receptor pathway do not resolve the whole site

facts.expectation: historic contamination should be managed using LCRM
facts.guard: completion of an early stage is not remediation verification

facts.part2a: guidance for legal determination and remediation under Part 2A
facts.guard: Part 2A legal determination is separate from planning-led redevelopment risk management

facts.controlled_waters: site-specific regulatory advice route exists where contamination has impacted controlled waters
facts.scope: service limitations and regulatory context must be checked
facts.guard: availability of advice is not a permit, approval or clean-site certificate

scope_guards: Brownfield or former industrial use is not treated as proof of unacceptable contamination.
Planning-led risk management and statutory Part 2A determination are kept separate.
A desk study is not treated as intrusive investigation or remediation verification.
Generic screening levels are not treated as a complete site-specific risk assessment.
Source, pathway and receptor must form a plausible pollutant linkage.
A remediation strategy is not treated as completed remediation.
Waste, water and environmental permits are not inferred from planning conditions.
No score or promotion is written without exact investigation, laboratory, remediation and verification evidence.
